title: The Ninth Door
description: Every map of Greykeep shows eight doors in the great hall. This morning there are nine — and the ninth has your name carved into the frame.

n1.caption: Every map of Greykeep shows eight doors in the great hall. This morning there are nine, and the ninth has your name carved into the frame.

n2a.caption: Beyond it: a library where every book is your life, written in hands that aren't yours. One volume on the desk is still being written.

n2b.caption: The steward goes pale. 'When the castle grows a door with your name, it is asking a question. Only you can answer it.'

n3a.caption: The last page is blank except one line: 'You may stop reading whenever you choose to start writing.' The quill beside it is still warm.

n3b.caption: You lift the unfinished book — and the shelves of your life begin unwriting themselves, spines going blank one by one.

n3c.caption: 'The question,' the steward whispers, 'is whether you want to know how your story ends. Those who open it never return the same.'
